security_audit.summary: Most static command-execution alerts are Markdown backtick and code-fence false positives; no prompt injection or hidden executable logic was found in SKILL.md. The skill still sends prompts and image references to third-party inference services and embeds one remote image asset.

remediation.suggestion: Add a clear notice that prompts, uploaded images, and image URLs are sent to inference.sh and model providers.
Replace the remote image with a packaged or marketplace-hosted asset to avoid viewer tracking and mutable content.
Label npx skill installation examples as optional and tell users to review each related skill before installing.

content.value_statement: Image teams need quick access to many generation and editing models without writing provider-specific workflows. This skill supplies belt CLI examples for text-to-image, edits, upscaling, and model selection.
actual_capabilities: Runs belt CLI examples for GPT-Image-2, FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, and other image apps.
Shows text-to-image prompts with quality, aspect ratio, and model-specific options.
Shows image editing and inpainting prompts using supplied image URLs.
Lists examples for upscaling and stitching image outputs.
Points users to model discovery and inference.sh documentation.
limitations: Requires an installed and authenticated inference.sh belt CLI.
Sends prompts and referenced images to external inference services.
Does not include local model weights or offline generation.
Model availability, pricing, and output quality depend on provider settings.

use_cases.title: Create Campaign Visuals
use_cases.description: Generate draft and final images for ads, landing pages, and social channels using model-specific prompts.

use_cases.title: Prototype Product Mockups
use_cases.description: Create studio-style product photos, edit backgrounds, and upscale selected outputs for review.

use_cases.title: Compare Image Models
use_cases.description: Test GPT-Image-2, FLUX, Gemini, Seedream, Reve, and Grok prompts from one CLI workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a square image of [subject] in [style] with [lighting] and [background]. Use a fast general image model.

prompt_templates.title: Edit a Product Photo
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this image URL: [image URL]. Change [specific element] to [new result] while preserving shape and perspective.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a model for [goal], [aspect ratio], [quality level], and [budget]. Then provide the belt command to run.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Campaign Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Create prompts for [campaign] across [formats]. Include model choices, aspect ratios, and editing steps for consistent visual style.

output_examples.input: Generate a studio product image for a matte black water bottle on a clean white background.
output_examples.output: A GPT-Image-2 workflow with a polished product prompt, high quality setting, and concise model rationale.

output_examples.input: Edit an existing shoe photo so the background becomes a beach at sunset.
output_examples.output: An image editing workflow that keeps the shoe unchanged and changes only the requested background scene.

output_examples.input: Find a fast model for a wide cyberpunk city image for a social banner.
output_examples.output: A FLUX or Grok workflow with a wide aspect ratio, prompt guidance, and expected tradeoffs.

best_practices: Confirm users approve sending prompts and image references to external services.
Use specific subject, style, lighting, camera, aspect ratio, and quality instructions.
Start with fast models for drafts, then use higher quality models for final images.
anti_patterns: Do not include private or regulated images unless the user approves third-party processing.
Do not ask for vague images when brand, style, or aspect ratio matters.
Do not install related skills automatically from the examples without explicit user approval.

faq.question: Does this skill require an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples require the belt CLI and an authenticated inference.sh account.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes image editing examples that use an image URL and a natural language edit prompt.

faq.question: Does it generate images locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses external inference.sh image apps, so generation happens outside the local environment.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Which image models are covered?
faq.answer: Examples include GPT-Image-2, FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, ImagineArt, and Topaz upscaling.

faq.question: Is user data sent to third parties?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts, image URLs, and uploaded images may be sent to inference.sh and model providers.
